content.title: Macy's strikes cautious tone on holiday sales, posts surprise profit
content.summary:
STORY: Macy’s is sounding cautious about this holiday season, even after it surprised Wall Street with a third-quarter profit.

The department store chain warned Wednesday that shoppers are becoming more selective as inflation pressures spending on non-essential items.

CEO Tony Spring said consumers are, quote, “discerning about how and where they spend their dollars.”

He noted that while Macy’s is “pleased” with the start of the holiday quarter, the retailer is being prudent with its expectations.

The comments mark the first from a retailer after the critical discount-heavy Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping period, which was driven by strong online sales, particularly from wealthy shoppers.

Looking ahead, Macy’s raised its full-year sales and profit outlook, helped by demand at its upscale Bloomingdale's label and the high-end beauty chain Bluemercury.

The company continues to invest in store refreshes and smaller formats as part of its turnaround plan.

content.title: Macy’s Posts Earnings Beat, but Consumers Are ‘Choiceful’ Heading Into Holiday
content.summary: Macy’s  the department store chain, topped third-quarter earnings expectations and posted its strongest same-store sales growth in 13 quarters.  Earnings guidance for the holiday quarter fell short of analysts’ estimates as the company takes what CEO Tony Spring calls a “prudent view” of the quarter.  Excited, but mindful that many aspirational customers in lower-middle-income households shop at  Macy’s  in the fourth quarter—customers that have proven to be value-focused and choiceful.
